raw_response:
I will still plant all 12 mu to cotton, same as last year. I do not like changing too much because one bad cotton year hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer money. On my side, with well water, I can push the crop a bit and not sit waiting for rain. I will do what has worked in our area and what I see other steady growers do: use a better seed than the old saved kind, plough the land first, put enough base fertilizer so the cotton does not stay weak, then add more nitrogen later when it starts growing hard. I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than watch the bolls stay small. But I also have only 2 people at home and 12 mu to manage, so I will keep the plan simple: one crop, a few irrigations at the key times, and spray when insects show up, not play around with too many fancy things.
